items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Names and exported docs are mostly clear. Some parts are obscure without comments: `isDefaultBatchDurable` compares function pointers via `reflect`, durations are clamped to `time.Nanosecond`, `close` is called twice in `DB.Close`, and the `durabilityJobSlot` fields have no docs.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: The new `durability.go` is 605 lines, over the 500-line cap. The expire/unblock logic for job slots is copy-pasted in `registerJob`, `recordCompletion` and `close`. `var _ = errorfs.ErrInjected` is left over in the test. Durability state is spread across 9 new `batchInternal` fields.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Errors are latched and channels are bounded. But `db.go` replaces `Logger.Fatalf` with `return err`, which can leave the commit pipeline stuck with a leaked semaphore. Durations are faked with `max(..., time.Nanosecond)`, and `close()` runs twice.

items.name: Commit path and public types remain backward compatible
items.name_zh: 提交路径与公共类型保持向后兼容
items.evidence: This changes existing behaviour. `applyInternal` used to call `d.opts.Logger.Fatalf("pebble: fatal commit error")` and now returns `err` for all commits. The `prepare` sync path (`b.commit.Add(2)`) is restructured. `registerJob` takes a global mutex on every sync commit even when BatchDurable is unset.
